reason: The text demonstrates agency among numerous non-leaders. Amnon (a prince but not yet a leader) actively plans and executes the assault on Tamar. Shimei independently curses and stones David. The woman from Tekoa uses her own wit and persuasion. Regular soldiers make choices about which faction to follow. Servants execute plans on their own initiative. The collective people counsel David against going to battle, influencing his decision. Even minor figures like Ziba and Ittai make deliberate choices that affect events. While leaders like David and Absalom certainly exercise greater agency with broader consequences, the narrative explicitly portrays non-leaders as actors with meaningful choice and independent action, not merely passive subjects.
